は.note: Marks what the sentence is about. Pronounced わ.

が.note: Marks the grammatical subject, or joins clauses as a soft 'but'.

を.note: Marks what the action is done to. Also marks the space moved through (空を飛ぶ).

に.note: Direction, location of existence, time point, or the receiver of an action.

へ.note: Direction of movement. Slightly more literary than に for destinations. Pronounced え.

で.note: Place where an action happens, or the tool/means used.

と.note: Accompaniment (友達と), exhaustive 'and', or marks quoted speech/thought before 言う・思う.

も.note: Replaces は・が・を to add 'also'. After a quantity: 'as much as'.

の.note: Links nouns (村の朝). Also turns a clause into a noun, and appears in explanatory のだ. Sentence-final (casual): どうしたの？ = what happened?; あたしが決めるの = I decide, that's all.

や.note: Lists examples without claiming completeness: AやBなど.

か.note: Marks questions, or 'or' between options. 〜かどうか = whether or not.

から.note: After a noun: starting point. After a clause: reason (casual-neutral).

まで.note: End point in time or space. までに = by (a deadline).

より.note: Comparison standard (AよりB). In formal writing, a stiff から.

だけ.note: Limits to exactly this. できるだけ = as much as possible.

しか.note: Always pairs with a negative: 一つしかない = there is only one.

など.short: and so on; the likes of
など.note: After examples. Can add dismissiveness: 俺など = someone like me.

ね.note: Seeks agreement or softens. Feminine/neutral depending on delivery.

よ.note: Asserts new information to the listener.

ぞ.note: Rough/masculine assertion, common in fiction. 行くぞ = we're going!

ぜ.note: Like ぞ but more casual-cocky. Strongly marks 'tough guy' speech in fiction.

さ.note: Casual 'you know'. Mid-sentence it marks a pause in very casual speech.

な.note: After plain verb: blunt prohibition (行くな). As なあ: musing emphasis.

わ.note: With rising tone: classic feminine speech (ですわ in お嬢様 role language). Falling tone: mild emphasis in many dialects. In 関西弁 men use it freely too: 拾ったるわ = I'll do it, then.

の?.note: Casual question marker, softer than か: 行くの？

こと.note: Turns a clause into an abstract 'fact/matter': 読むこと = (the act of) reading.

もの.note: A tangible thing. Sentence-final もの/もん = 'because~' with a pleading tone.

ところ.note: Physical place, or aspect: 食べたところ = just ate; 食べるところ = about to eat.

とき.note: Clause + とき = 'when ~'. Tense before it is relative to the main clause.

まえ.note: Noun の前 / verb-dictionary form + 前に = before doing.

あと.note: た-form + あとで = after doing.

ため.short: for the sake of; because of
ため.note: Purpose (〜ために = in order to) or cause, depending on context.

はず.note: Logical expectation: 来るはずだ = he should be coming (I have reason to believe).

わけ.note: というわけだ = so that's why. わけではない = it's not that~.

つもり.note: Dictionary form + つもり = plan to. た-form + つもり = believe (perhaps wrongly) that one did.

そう.note: そうだ/そうですね as agreement. (As verb-stem + そう see the aux entry.)

よう.note: 〜のようだ = seems/like. ように = so that / as. ようとする = try to.

らしい.note: Hearsay/inference from outside info; or 'befitting' (男らしい).

みたい.note: Casual counterpart of ようだ: 夢みたいだ = it's like a dream.

です.note: Polite 'is'. Past でした, negative ではありません/じゃないです.

ます.note: Verb stem + ます. Past ました, negative ません.

だ.note: Plain 'is'. Dropped in casual female speech, kept in male/blunt speech.

じゃ.note: Role language: elderly or rural characters use じゃ where standard speech uses だ. そうじゃ = that's right. Core of the 'old wizard' register.

ではない.note: Formal negative copula. Spoken casual: じゃない.

じゃない.note: Casual negative copula. Rising tone turns it into 'isn't it?'.

ている.note: Progressive (食べている = is eating) or state (知っている = knows). Casual contraction: てる.

てる.note: Spoken contraction of ている. Everywhere in casual dialogue and media.

ておる.note: Role language: ている in the old-person register (わし知っておる). Also humble in business keigo (存じております).

ちゃう.note: Contraction of てしまう: 食べちゃった = ate it all up / went and ate it. Casual speech staple.

ちまう.note: Rough-masculine contraction of てしまう: 死んじまう. Marks tough/downtown speech in fiction.

てしまう.note: Completion or regret: 忘れてしまった = went and forgot.

ておく.note: Do and leave done, in preparation: 買っておく. Contraction: とく.

てみる.note: Do and see what happens: 聞いてみる = try asking.

てくる.note: Movement toward speaker, or a change arriving: 見えてくる = come into view.

ていく.note: Movement away, or continuing into the future: 変わっていく.

てくれる.note: Someone does the action as a favor toward the speaker's side.

てもらう.note: Receive the favor of someone doing: 見てもらう = have (them) look at it.

てあげる.note: Do as a favor outward. Can sound condescending if overused.

られる.note: Context decides: is done to (passive), can do (potential), or subject-honorific.

させる.note: Causative: 行かせる = make/let (them) go.

ない.note: Plain negative. Stem for many patterns: なければ, なくて, ず.

たい.note: Verb stem + たい. Third-person wants usually take たがる or らしい.

なければならない.note: Obligation. Spoken contractions: なきゃ, なくちゃ.

ねばならぬ.note: Literary/archaic 'must'. Role language for old or stiffly formal characters; also in proverbs and period drama.

なきゃ.note: Contraction of なければ(ならない): 行かなきゃ = gotta go.

かもしれない.note: Possibility. Polite: かもしれません. Casual: かも.

かも.note: Clipped かもしれない. Very common in speech.

だろう.note: Conjecture. Rising tone: seeking agreement (だろ？ in male speech).

でしょう.note: Polite だろう. Rising でしょう？ = right?

まい.note: Literary negative conjecture (あるまい = probably isn't) or negative volition (二度と行くまい = I shall never go again).

べき.note: Dictionary form + べき(だ) = should, by principle. するべき→すべき.

はずがない.note: Strong logical denial: 彼が来るはずがない.

ことができる.note: Dictionary form + ことができる. Stiffer than the short potential form.

ことになる.note: Outcome decided by circumstance/others. ことにする = decide oneself.

ようになる.note: Gradual change of state/ability: 読めるようになった.

ようとする.note: Volitional + とする: attempt or the moment just before an action.

たとたん.note: た-form + とたん(に): the moment X happened, Y (unexpected) happened.

かけの.note: Stem + かけ(の/だ): started but unfinished. 読みかけの本 = half-read book.

ずに.note: Literary ないで: 眠らずに歩いた = walked without sleeping. する→せずに.

ばかり.note: た-form + ばかり = just happened. Verb + てばかり = does nothing but.

んばかりに.note: Literary: 泣かんばかりに = as if on the verge of tears. ない-stem + んばかり.

ながら.note: Stem + ながら = while doing. 〜ながらも = despite being.

ば.note: Hypothetical condition: 行けば分かる = if you go, you'll see.

たら.note: The most conversational conditional; also 'when X happened, (I found) Y'.

なら.note: Takes the topic as given: 行くなら今だ = if you're going, now's the time.

ったら.note: Casual exasperated topic marker: お父さんったら！ Mostly feminine/familiar speech.

のに.note: Contrast with frustration: 言ったのに = even though I told you.

ても.note: て-form + も: concession. 何度読んでも = no matter how many times I read.

のだ.note: Written explanatory tone. Spoken: んだ/んです. Questions: のか/の？

んだ.note: Spoken のだ: adds 'the thing is...'. んだよ, んだけど etc.

わけではない.note: Partial denial: 嫌いなわけではない = it's not that I dislike it.

ざるを得ない.note: Literary: ない-stem + ざるを得ない. する→せざるを得ない.

ゆえに.note: Literary 'because/thus'. Noun + ゆえ(に) appears in fantasy and formal writing.

ものの.note: Concession in writing: 買ったものの使っていない.

つつ.note: Literary ながら. 〜つつある = in the process of.

において.note: Formal で: 王都において = in the capital.

によって.note: Agent of passive, cause, or 'varies by'.

として.note: 弟子として = as an apprentice.

にとって.note: 私にとって = for me / as far as I'm concerned.

について.note: Topic of discussion: 塔について = about the tower.

だが.note: Written narration or blunt male speech.

でも.note: Sentence-initial casual 'but'. After a noun: 'even' or 'or something' (お茶でも).

それなら.note: Picking up the other person's statement as a premise.

まさか.note: Disbelief: まさか…！ Often with negative or まい.

おい.note: Masculine attention-getter. Rude outside close/rough relationships.

わし.note: First person pronoun of the old-man register in fiction. Pairs with じゃ・〜ておる.

おれ.note: 俺. Casual-masculine first person: friends, rivals, tough speech.

あたし.note: Softened わたし used in casual feminine speech.

ございます.note: Polite ある: 〜でございます is the formal copula of service/court speech.

いらっしゃる.note: Honorific for いる・来る・行く, raising the subject. ます-form: いらっしゃいます.

おっしゃる.note: Honorific 言う. おっしゃいました = (someone esteemed) said.

いたす.note: Humble する, lowering the speaker: お願いいたします.

おる.note: Humble いる in keigo (おります); plain おる in the elderly register.

かしこまりました.note: Service/retainer speech for 'understood'. Stiffer than 分かりました.

かねます.note: Stem + かねます: business-polite 'cannot': いたしかねます.

ませ.note: いらっしゃいませ、くださいませ: the ます-imperative of service and court speech.

てはならない.note: Formal prohibition, common in narration and rules: 近づいてはならない.

のである.note: Written のだ: marks the sentence as explanation or conclusion of what preceded. Classic novel-narration ending.

いけない.note: てはいけない = must not; なきゃいけない = must. Alone: 'oh no / that's bad'.

なんて.note: Marks disbelief or belittling: 塔が生えるなんて = (the very idea) that a tower would sprout.

だい.note: どこへ行くんだい？ Familiar, slightly old-fashioned question ending, typical of parents and grandparents in fiction.

かい.note: 元気かい？ Softer than か, old-fashioned or avuncular.

のう.note: Old-person register: そうじゃのう = hmm, indeed. The elderly counterpart of ねえ.

さま.note: 様. Court and service speech, or reverence.

じゃねえ.note: Rough-masculine じゃない: 冗談じゃねえ = this is no joke. Unrelated to the old-man copula じゃ.

じゃねえか.note: Rough-masculine 〜じゃないか: confirmation or protest. いいじゃねえか = come on, it's fine!

ねえ.note: In rough speech ない flattens to ねえ: 知らねえ = dunno. Drawn-out ねえ at the start of a sentence is just 'hey'.

てくれ.note: Blunt-masculine てください: 待ってくれ = wait!

だろ.note: Clipped だろう, rising tone: 言っただろ = I told you, didn't I?

ですわ.note: お嬢様 role language: です + feminine わ. Marks elegant female speech in fiction; rare in real life.

のじゃ.note: The old-person register's んだ: そうなのじゃ = that's how it is, you see.

おぬし.note: Archaic second person; sages, samurai, and period fiction.

ふむ.note: Thoughtful grunt; bookish or elderly characters.

てはいけない.note: Standard prohibition: 触ってはいけない.

なさい.note: Stem + なさい: parental/teacherly imperative. 食べなさい.

ください.note: をください = please give; てください = please do.

ございません.note: Negative of ございます: 申し訳ございません.

いたします.note: Humble する in its polite form: お願いいたします.

おります.note: Humble います; also 〜ております for 〜ています in formal speech.

ございました.note: ありがとうございました etc.

いらっしゃいます.note: Polite form of いらっしゃる.

申し上げます.note: Very humble 言う; also お〜申し上げます pattern in court/business speech.

存じます.note: Humble 思う/知る: ありがたく存じます.

かのよう.note: Plain form + かのように (adverb) / かのような (+ noun) / かのようだ: describes something by comparing it to what it is not. 時が止まったかのように = as if time had stopped. A narrator's favourite.

ずにはいられない.note: ない-stem + ずにはいられない (する → せずには): an urge you can't hold back. 笑わずにはいられない = can't help laughing.

わけにはいかない.note: Dictionary form + わけにはいかない: impossible for social, moral or situational reasons — not lack of ability. 負けるわけにはいかない = I can't afford to lose. Negative + わけにはいかない = have to.

ので.note: Softer and more objective than から.

という.note: Quotes or names: ニコという少年 = a boy called Niko. Sentence-final 〜という = 'it is said'.

って.short: (casual quote/topic) — = と / という / は
って.note: Spoken shorthand: 行くって = (he) said he's going; ニコって = this Niko / Niko is…

ってば.note: Casual, impatient: 起きてるってば！ = I'm up, I told you!

まま.short: as is; still (in the same state)
まま.note: 指したまま = still pointing; そのまま = just as it is.

ほど.short: to the extent of; about; the more…
ほど.note: 死ぬほど = to the point of dying; 三日ほど = about three days.

くらい.short: about; at least; to the extent that

かしら.note: Traditional feminine かな. Common in お嬢様 speech and older women's speech in fiction.

わよ.note: わ + よ: firm but feminine. Strong お嬢様/older-lady flavour in fiction.

ですの.note: お嬢様 role language: です + の, either as a soft explanation or a question (ですの？).

ますの.note: Polite ます + の: refined feminine explanation/question.

こそ.note: Emphasises the word before it: ニコこそ = Niko, you're the one (who should talk).

ずつ.note: ひとつずつ = one by one.

わたくし.note: The most formal first person. In fiction, the signature pronoun of noble young ladies.

やん.note: 関西弁 = じゃない / じゃん.

やねん.note: 関西弁 や (= だ) + ねん (explanatory).

ねん.note: 関西弁: 行くねん = 行くんだ.

へん.note: 関西弁: わからへん = わからない; でけへん = できない.

しゃあない.short: can't be helped (Kansai しょうがない)

のよう.note: Noun + のように (adverb) / のような (+ noun) / のようだ: likeness or resemblance. 紙のように = like paper.

ますので.note: ます + ので: polite explanatory reason.

ですので.note: です + ので: polite reason; also sentence-initial ですので = therefore.

のかしら.note: の + かしら: feminine, often a little sarcastic in お嬢様 speech.

からには.note: Plain form + からには: having committed to X, you're obliged to follow through. 約束したからには守る = having promised, I keep it.

どころか.note: X どころか Y: not only not X, but (the opposite) Y. 褒められるどころか怪しまれる = far from being praised, I'm suspected.

に違いない.note: Plain form + に違いない: strong conviction from evidence. Written/narrative flavour.

にもかかわらず.note: Plain form / noun + にもかかわらず: something happens contrary to what you'd expect. Formal; also sentence-initial: にもかかわらず、… = and yet.

以来.note: て-form / noun + 以来: from that point on, continuing to now. 母がいなくなって以来 = ever since Mom disappeared.

のかもしれない.note: の (explanatory) + かもしれない: perhaps the situation is that ~.

わけがない.note: Plain form + わけがない: flat logical impossibility. 戻ってくるわけがない = it can't possibly come back. Casual: わけない.

にすぎない.note: Noun / plain form + にすぎない: downplays something as small or insignificant. 噂にすぎない = it's only a rumour.

ばかりか.note: X ばかりか Y (も/さえ/まで): not just X, but on top of that Y — usually escalating. Written register.

たまえ.note: Verb stem + たまえ: superior-to-inferior command. Old-fashioned aristocratic/boss speech.

しかない.short: have no choice but to; nothing but
しかない.note: Dictionary form + しかない: the only option left.

でして.short: (polite) is, and… / it's that… (て-form of です)
でして.note: Polite connective: 仲でしてね = we were (classmates), you see.

をめぐって.note: Noun + をめぐって / をめぐる + noun: the issue around which conflict, debate or competition revolves.

からといって.note: Plain form + からといって, usually followed by a negative: X is true, but X alone doesn't justify the conclusion.

に対して.note: Noun + に対して: the target of an action/attitude, or a contrast between two things.

わけだ.short: so that's why; it follows that ~
わけだ.note: Plain form + わけだ: a conclusion that naturally follows from what's known, or the 'aha' of understanding a reason.

とは限らない.note: Plain form + とは限らない: it isn't always/necessarily so. Often with 必ずしも or からといって.

ないことはない.short: it's not that ~ not (= it's possible, sort of)
ないことはない.note: Double negative: できないことはない = it's not impossible / I could, I suppose. Hedged, reluctant yes.
